newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk commission reaches wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk commission reaches wage deal.

text.p: A commission seeking to defuse a labour dispute at Russia's Norilsk Nickel combine has agreed a salary arrears repayment schedule designed to avert possible disruptions at the plant, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

It said that a reconciliation commission, representing labour and management and dominated by trade union representives, had approved a schedule under which October 1996 salaries to workers at the flagship combine would be paid off on Tuesday and November 1996 arrears by next month.
All arrears and other debts to workers would be fully paid off by the end of the year, it said.

Plant workers have given RAO Norilsky Nickel 0#NKEL.RUO NKEL.RTS management until February 20 to pay off wage arrears, raise the minimum monthly wage to 500,000 roubles and secure financing for all workers' privileges and guarantees.
Total salary arrears are around one trillion roubles.

Interfax did not say whether the commission had agreed a wage rise, which Norilsk officials have said would cost the cash-strapped producer of nickel, copper and precious metals an extra 70 billion roubles a month.
